Confirmed: site is test rbx,rbx; je 0x14462aff8 follows; rbx=[[r12+0x28]+0xe0]; rax=[r12+0x58] nonzero (je 0x14462a6fc otherwise) and live at aff8, whose first insn is or byte[rax+0x224],1 with no reload; R allocated 0x3bf60 align 0x10 in 0x14463adc0 and stored at world+0xe0; count u32 +0x5d8; 26 slots: 0x5e0 and 0x6b0 8-byte arrays, 0x396c0 array stride 0x190 ends exactly at 0x3bf60; 0x14462a978 mov qword [rbx+rdx*2-4],0 = R+0x396c0+i*0x190 so slot 26 writes 8 bytes at R+0x3bf60 (past the end) in the R+0x350==0 zero-fill loop (a921 path, clears slots 0..newcount-1 then jmp aff3); count only incs at a933 and afe0 (sim path). Skipping is safe as far as traced: lock [R+0x24768] entered at a67d and released at afed only inside the skipped region, 0x24750 zeroed only there; registration index is stored only into R (0x5e0 and 0xd148 arrays), never into the car or phys; from aff8 to ret at 0x14462b7d5 rbx is always written before any read and R is never read. WRONG/IMPRECISE: (1) aff8 onwards only sets bits 0-5 of [rax+0x224]: true only for the first six insns (1,2,4,8,0x10,0x20); Car_Chassis_Build continues (r12+0x38, call 0x14462d090 ...). (2) the R+0x3bf60 OOB write is specific to the zero-fill path; the sim path for the 27th (r14=26) writes inside R but into the neighbouring arrays (0x5e0+26*8=0x6b0, xmm at 0xd220+26*16=0xd3c0) and indexes scheduler arrays at [R+0x350]+0xa5f9b0+26*4, so it corrupts rather than overruns. Not exhaustively proven: other consumers of the registry (scheduler iterating count slots) were not traced.
